etymology.root: French meunier, miller — from the floury white hairs on the leaves

text.what: Pinot noir with white down on its shoot tips and leaves — meunier means miller, and the vine looks dusted with flour. It buds later, ripens earlier and survives a frosty Champagne spring that kills its parent.
text.how: Genetically it is a chimera: two tissue layers, each carrying its own mutation, neither identical to pinot noir. Propagate it from the wrong layer and you get something else.
text.today: Champagne plants it heavily in the frost-prone Marne valley, and a handful of growers now bottle it alone.

kin.as: The vine it mutated from, and cannot be a parent of.
Where it earns its keep: the valley floors that frost.
A press-house decision that treats it the same as its parent.
